# PM CARES Fund — Facts, Figures & Timeline

> Independent, non-commercial public-information page about India's PM CARES Fund.
> Article-sourced figures come from the English Wikipedia article
> (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PM_CARES_Fund, accessed 16 August 2026).
> The FY2024-25 audited-statement block additionally comes from the fund's own
> published statement (https://pmcares.gov.in/assets/donation/pdf/Audited_Statement_2024_25.pdf,
> accessed 28 August 2026).
> Criticism and the government's defence are presented side by side; no editorial verdict.

URL: https://pm-cares-fund-information.vercel.app/

## Key facts

- Full name: Prime Minister's Citizen Assistance and Relief in Emergency Situations Fund; created 27 March 2020 during the COVID-19 pandemic; registered public charitable trust (New Delhi) whose trust deed describes it as a private trust.
- Chaired by the Prime Minister (Narendra Modi); Defence, Home and Finance ministers are ex-officio trustees. Operates from the PMO, South Block. Minimum donation ₹10.
- Money received: ₹3,076.62 crore in the last five days of FY2019-20 and ₹7,913.55 crore of new money in FY2020-21 — the widely-quoted ₹10,990.17 crore is that year's receipts-side total including the opening balance (per the fund's own statement). Year-end balance 31 March 2021: ₹7,013.99 crore. Across the six audited years (FY2019-20 → FY2024-25): receipts ₹16,598.87 crore, payments ₹8,146.81 crore (both derived).
- First allocation, 13 May 2020: ₹3,100 crore — 50,000 made-in-India ventilators (₹2,000 cr share is derived arithmetic), ₹1,000 crore for migrant-worker welfare via states, ₹100 crore for vaccine-development support.
- Audit: private chartered accountants SARC & Associates (appointed June 2020) signed FY2021-22 (UDIN 22084884AXGCSU1642, 30 Sep 2022) and FY2022-23 (UDIN 24084884BKIKDZ2614, 29 Mar 2024) — four financial years in total (Frontline's count); KKC & Associates LLP (formerly Khimji Kunverji & Co LLP) signed FY2023-24 and FY2024-25 (7 Aug 2026). The CAG does not audit the fund. Neither KKC statement displays a UDIN (flagged by CA Atul Modani as a correctable oversight, India Today).
- Latest balance (audited, primary source): ₹8,452.07 crore on 31 March 2025 (savings ₹605.41 cr + fixed deposits ₹7,846.65 cr). FY2024-25: receipts ₹1,279.91 cr (derived: printed total ₹8,452.95 cr − opening ₹7,173.03 cr; incl. ₹469.38 cr fixed-deposit interest), payments ₹0.88 cr (₹87,85,291 — PM CARES for Children ₹87,84,840 + bank/SMS charges ₹451), ₹324.66 cr refunded by implementing agencies. FY2023-24 closing balance: ₹7,173.03 cr.
- RTI: the PMO refused RTI requests and told the Delhi High Court the fund is "not a public authority"; critics cite the national emblem and ministerial trustees to argue otherwise.
- FCRA: exempted from all FCRA 2010 provisions, permitting foreign contributions; corporate donations counted as CSR; 80G income-tax exemption for donations before 30 June 2020.
- Delivery gaps reported: only 2,923 of 50,000 ventilators made by 24 June 2020; of 162 sanctioned oxygen plants, 11 installed (5 operational) per Scroll (April 2021) vs a government claim of 33; for Delhi, 8 sanctioned, 1 built (told to the Delhi High Court, 22 April 2021).

## Six-year audited record (FY2019-20 → FY2024-25, primary tier)

Closing balance / receipts-during / payments, ₹ crore, all identity-verified against the statements:
- 2019–20: 3,076.62 / 3,076.62 / 0 — statement: https://pmcares.gov.in/assets/donation/pdf/Audited%20Statement.PDF
- 2020–21: 7,013.99 / 7,913.55 (derived) / 3,976.17 — statement: https://pmcares.gov.in/assets/donation/pdf/Audited_Statement_2020_21.pdf
- 2021–22: 5,415.66 / 2,117.95 (derived) / 3,716.29 — statement: https://pmcares.gov.in/assets/donation/pdf/Audited_Statement_2021_22.pdf
- 2022–23: 6,283.68 / 1,305.90 (derived) / 437.87 (PM CARES for Children 346.00 + 99,986 oxygen concentrators 91.87) — statement: https://pmcares.gov.in/assets/donation/pdf/Audited_Statement_2022_23.pdf
- 2023–24: 7,173.03 / 904.94 (derived) / 15.60 — statement: https://pmcares.gov.in/assets/donation/pdf/Audited_Statement_2023_24.pdf
- 2024–25: 8,452.07 / 1,279.91 (derived) / 0.88 (₹87,85,291) — statement below.
Domestic donations declined every year: 7,183.78 → 1,896.76 → 908.13 → 681.81 → 479.05 crore; foreign: 494.92 → 40.12 → 2.57 → 1.13 → 0.93 crore.

## News tier — August 2026 coverage

The FY2023-24 + FY2024-25 statements were released together on 18 August 2026 after a ~2-year disclosure gap (The Hindu reported the gap 8 Aug 2026; FY2023-24 finalized ~28 months after year-end). Reactions, attributed: NCPRI's Anjali Bhardwaj ("utilised only 0.01% of available ₹8,452 crore", "shrouded in secrecy"); Cmde Lokesh Batra (retd) (accumulation "over ₹8,000 crore, with little money spent"); CHRI's Venkatesh Nayak ("'need to know' disclosure era", urges CAG performance audit); Congress ("₹8,452 crore sitting idle while people suffer"). Government position (The Telegraph): the fund is reserved for crises and national emergencies; fixed deposits are a cushion earning returns. PM CARES for Children (announced 30 May 2022) is the fund's only recorded programme spending FY2023-24 → FY2024-25 (FY2022-23 also paid ₹91.87 crore for 99,986 oxygen concentrators). The Hindu calculates cumulative spending at 18.4% of total income (news-derived, not recomputed here).

## Primary source — audited FY2024-25 statement

- URL: https://pmcares.gov.in/assets/donation/pdf/Audited_Statement_2024_25.pdf (accessed 28 August 2026)
- Audited by KKC & Associates LLP (formerly Khimji Kunverji & Co LLP), FRN 105146W/W100621; report dated 7 August 2026.
- Receipts totals are derived from the statements' printed totals; itemized lines are as printed. FY2022-23 and FY2023-24 rows are verified against the fund's separately published statements for those years (URLs in the six-year section).
- Shown separately from Wikipedia-sourced figures; the two tiers are never mixed in one chart or total.

## Data caveats

Estimates (e.g., the ₹10,600 crore two-month total and 53/42/5 donor mix) are labeled as
estimates; derived arithmetic is labeled as derived; month-level dates are shown where the
article gives no day. The Wikipedia article is tagged "needs update (July 2026)".
